body.x: WORLD'S SMALLEST PROGRAMMABLE ROBOT RETURNS TO CES A HIT WITH KIDS, TECH GEEKS & EDUCATORS

Evollve (www.Ozobot.com), a company built around an idea that blends physical and digital technologies to provide social, educational and competitive applications with a core foundation of instilling valuable life skills, introduced Ozobot at CES Unveiled, a pre-show of CES 2015 which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

Ozobot is the world's smallest programmable robot with the intuitive color-based language. Designed for ages 8 and above, it can sense colored lines, detect patterns such as intersections, read flashing light codes and play back up to 500 commands. It's mostly based on the hardware design of the original Ozobot but Bit is programmable via both color-based code language and a block-based programming editor based on Blockly. It can move at speeds up to 3.5 inches/sec (8.5 cm/sec) and it operates on physical surfaces such as paper and game boards and digital screens such as tablets and mobile phones.

“We are establishing Ozobot as a platform built around programmable robots that fuse together learning and playing,” explains Evollve's CTO, Armen Kroyan, PhD. “Ozobot’s small size, intelligence and versatility make it into the ultimate smart game piece that plays in both physical and digital worlds." She also said, "On the STEM learning and programming side, children at a young age get an introduction to basic programming concepts, logic and deductive reasoning using Ozobot’s intuitive and easy-to-grasp color-based code language. Older kids and adults can learn programming and access Ozobot’s more advanced capabilities using our block-based programming editor based on Google’s Blockly.”

Ozobot made its debut at CES in January 2014 with warm welcome from kids, grownups and the media for filling the gap between virtual and digital play. It received 10 industry awards and nominated for a Toy of the Year (TOTY) in the Most Innovative Toy category from the Toy Industry Association. Also, it will receive 2015 Kids at Play Interactive (KAPi) award for Best Robot. The preview of new robots to be released in 2015, Ozobot Bit and Ozobot Jot, are on pre-sale at the booth.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
